title: Canada and U.S. Trade Fight: Tariffs Are Like a Tax on Stuff
summary:
Have you ever had a fight with a friend and both of you said, "I'm not talking to you!"? That's kind of what's happening between the United States and Canada right now.

Canada's Prime Minister, Mark Carney, says the U.S. is putting new taxes on things from Canada, like steel, dairy, and electronics. These taxes are called tariffs. Carney says this is a "miscalculation"—a big mistake—and it's meant to hurt Canada.

So Canada is fighting back. Starting September 8, Canada will put tariffs on American goods too, dollar-for-dollar. That means if the U.S. taxes Canadian steel $100, Canada taxes American steel $100.

Carney said he walked away from a deal because he didn't want to give up Canada's independence. He felt the U.S. was attacking Canada. The U.S. says Canada made last-minute changes and new demands. Now, the U.S. trade representative says there are no plans to talk again.

Tariffs can make things more expensive for everyone. Some people think they help American factories, but others say they just raise prices for families. Many Canadians are even boycotting American products—choosing not to buy them.

It's a big mess, and nobody knows when it will end.
why_it_matters: This matters because tariffs can raise the prices of things your family buys, from food to electronics, so a trade fight between neighboring countries can affect your home budget.
